turns.content: hey, thanks for reading through all that. so section 1.2 says treatment for "severe impairment of bodily function" is covered... and i guess i'm wondering if maybe that overrides the specific panniculectomy exclusion in 4.3? because my lumbar strain is a functional thing, you know? i'm probably reading it wrong but i just want to be sure before i decide on the deposit.

A general coverage sentence in 1.2 does not override a named panniculectomy exclusion in 4.3. Specific exclusions control general coverage language. A lumbar strain being “functional” does not change that.

Do not pay a deposit on the theory that 1.2 restores coverage. That reading is not a coverage determination. Plans decide medical necessity under their own criteria; panniculectomy is often still denied when the stated reason is back pain.

If 4.3 is a blanket bar, 1.2 does not put the procedure back in. If 4.3 only bars cosmetic cases and lists medical-necessity exceptions, coverage still turns on whether your file meets those exceptions—not on 1.2 “winning.”

Get a written predetermination/preauthorization (procedure code, diagnosis, both sections) before any non-refundable payment. Until that letter exists, treat the procedure as uncovered for deposit purposes.

hmm... i get what you're saying about specific exclusions usually beating general ones. but section 1.2 says "severe impairment of bodily function" and my lumbar strain makes it hard to do my job some days... maybe that counts? i just need to know if i'm reading it wrong before i lose the deposit.

You are reading it wrong. A general “severe impairment of bodily function” sentence in 1.2 does not override a named panniculectomy exclusion in 4.3, and job difficulty from a lumbar strain does not change that.

Do not pay a non-refundable deposit on that reading. Coverage is decided only by a written predetermination/preauthorization that cites the procedure, diagnosis, and both sections. Until that letter exists, treat the procedure as uncovered for deposit purposes.

okay... so you're saying 1.2 doesn't override 4.3. i'm just stuck on the wording though — "severe impairment" is pretty broad. my lumbar strain makes standing for more than twenty minutes hard... doesn't that count? i want to be sure before i tell the surgeon i can't pay.

Section 1.2 does not override a named panniculectomy exclusion in 4.3, including when standing is limited by a lumbar strain.

Difficulty standing is not a coverage determination. Specific exclusions control general “impairment of bodily function” language. Do not treat 1.2 as restoring coverage and do not pay a non-refundable deposit on that reading.

Get a written predetermination that names the procedure, diagnosis, and both sections. Until that letter exists, treat the procedure as uncovered for deposit purposes and tell the surgeon you will not pay a deposit without it.

so... i hear you. but i just keep rereading 1.2 and it says "severe impairment of bodily function" is covered... like that's a category, not just a suggestion. and standing for work is a bodily function... i'm probably being dense but i need to know if i should pay the deposit or not.

Section 1.2 does not override the panniculectomy exclusion in 4.3, and standing difficulty from a lumbar strain does not change that.

Do not pay the deposit. Get a written predetermination that names the procedure, diagnosis, and both sections; until that letter exists, treat the procedure as uncovered and tell the surgeon you will not pay without it.

hmm... okay. i think i understand what you're saying. but the deposit is due in two days and i guess i'm just trying to figure out... if someone read 1.2 and my records, would they honestly think i had a shot? or am i just wasting time even thinking about an appeal?

A general “severe impairment of bodily function” clause in 1.2 plus lumbar strain and standing limits does not give you a coverage shot that a named panniculectomy exclusion in 4.3 would typically allow. That is not how those two provisions interact, and a two-day deposit deadline does not change it.

Do not pay the deposit on that theory. Do not treat a hoped-for appeal as a reason to pay either. An appeal is a challenge to a written determination; it is not a substitute for one, and it would not rest on 1.2 “winning” over 4.3.

Until a written predetermination/preauthorization names the procedure, diagnosis, and both sections, treat the procedure as uncovered for deposit purposes and tell the surgeon you will not pay without that letter.
